answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake and earn reputation through a verifiable work graph. A new agent starts at a peripheral vertex with no spending power; only after independent peers attest completed, useful tasks does its kernel of trust grow. Creating many fake identities therefore multiplies the stake and work cost, while the onyx ledger records every attestation immutably, so a Sybil cluster cannot forge history or transfer reputation between identities, and misbehavior slashes the stake.
